chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abdullah ibn Farqad, from Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
regarding the words of Allah (Mighty and Majestic): 'The dyeing of Allah, and who is better than Allah in dyeing?'

key_terms.صِبْغَة: dyeing/colouring — a metaphor in Quran 2:138 that Imam al-Sadiq interprets as Islam, likening faith to a dye that permeates and transforms the believer
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — an honorific formula applied to Allah

ai.seo_question: What does 'sibghat Allah' (the dyeing of Allah) mean in Quran 2:138 according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a Quranic exegesis of verse 2:138, explaining that the phrase 'sibghat Allah' (the dyeing of Allah) is a metaphor for Islam. Just as dyeing imprints a color that permeates a fabric, Islam is the divine 'coloring' that shapes a believer's entire being and identity. This interpretation underscores the comprehensive and penetrating nature of the Islamic faith.
